description: Sync page text from selected Notion pages and databases, one document per page. Database properties other than titles are not synced.
opening: Sync the Notion databases and top-level pages you share with the connector's integration. Each page is one document: a database row, a selected page, and every sub-page under them. Each sub-page links to the page it sits under.

A database row brings in its title and page text only. Status, owner, dates, tags and other properties are not read. Notion page sharing is not imported, so every synced page is visible to everyone who can query the collection unless you set an access rule. Pages deleted or unshared in Notion stay in HydraDB.

connect.auth: Notion uses an internal integration token.

credentials.name: access_token
credentials.text: A Notion internal integration token. It starts with `secret_` or `ntn_`.

permissions.name: Read content
permissions.text: required. Lets HydraDB search, read pages and blocks, and query databases.

permissions.name: Read user information without email
permissions.text: optional. Lets HydraDB check the token and show who created a page.

steps.title: Create an integration
steps.text: In Notion, create an internal integration with the Read content capability, and copy its token.

steps.title: Share content with it
steps.text: Share each database and page you want synced with the integration. HydraDB can list only what the integration can see.

steps.title: Select resources
steps.text: HydraDB lists every database the integration can see, and every page that sits at the top of the workspace. Select at least one database or top-level page.

connect.account: One connector reads what one integration can see.

sync.first_sync: A database reaches back 30 days by last edited time by default, set by `lookback_days`. A selected page and its sub-pages are read again on every sync.
sync.changes: For a database, rows edited since the last sync are read again in full, with their sub-pages. For a selected page, the whole page tree is read on every sync, and the pages edited since the last sync are sent.
sync.edits: For a directly selected page tree, edited pages replace their existing documents on the next sync. For a sub-page under a database row, the change is picked up only when the database row is also edited.
sync.deletes: Pages deleted or unshared in Notion are not removed. They stay searchable in HydraDB.
notes: Sub-pages are followed up to 10 levels deep, and blocks up to 20 levels deep.
If a sub-page or block is unavailable, its content is omitted. Other accessible content on the page can still sync.

documents.name: Pages
documents.one_document: One Notion page: a database row, a selected page, or any sub-page under them. A sub-page is its own document, not part of its parent's text.
documents.title: The page's title. A page without a title uses its Notion id.
documents.text: The page title at the top, the creator as an `Author` line, and the plain text of the page's blocks in order, one block per line: paragraphs, headings, bulleted and numbered lists, to-dos, toggles, quotes, callouts and code. Text inside toggles and callouts is included.
documents.date: When the page was last edited.
documents.files: Images and files remain links to the originals. Image text is searchable only when image reading is available in your deployment. Do not rely on PDF or Word attachment text being searchable.

attributes.name: created_by
attributes.text: The creator's display name, or their Notion id if the name cannot be read. It is the `Author` line of the text, and the graph records the page as written by that person.

attributes.name: last_edited_time
attributes.text: When the page was last edited. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.notion_page_id
attributes.text: The page's Notion id. Limits a query to one page. Not searchable.

attributes.name: connector_id
attributes.text: Limits a query to this connector's pages. Not searchable.

attributes.name: parent_id
attributes.text: For a sub-page, the page it sits under. Links the two, so a page tree is connected in the graph. Not searchable.

attributes.name: created_by_email
attributes.text: The creator's email, when Notion returns one. It lets the graph recognise the same person across tools. Not searchable.

attributes.name: mentions
attributes.text: People @mentioned in the page. The graph records each as mentioned by the page. The field itself is not searchable, but the page text it comes from is.

attributes.name: last_edited_by
attributes.text: The Notion user id of the last editor. It is not turned into a name or a person.

example_searches: What does our onboarding page say about laptop setup?
Which Notion pages did Priya create?
What sub-pages sit under the Engineering Handbook page?

connections: A sub-page to the page it sits under.
No links from Notion pages to other tools. In the other direction, GitHub issues, pull requests and comments that link to a Notion page are linked to it.
people: The page's creator, with an email when Notion returns one.
graph.from_text: The page text, including people and projects named in plain text rather than @mentioned. Database properties are not read, so anything kept only in database columns cannot be found.

not_synced: Property values other than the title, such as status, owner, dates and tags, are not read.
Pages and databases not shared with the integration.
Text in unsupported blocks, such as table rows, equations, embeds and bookmarks.
Deletions: deleted pages stay in HydraDB.
